_comment: Prose contrast per country for the compare page (src/compare.njk), rendered as the 'How these differ' block above each country's table. Keyed by the bare country slug used in countryGroups.js. Intentionally qualitative (vibe, swim, cost tier, route, ease) and free of rank numbers so it survives re-ranking — see CLAUDE.md's note on editorial prose that cites ranks. Only countries with 2+ live options need an entry. HTML allowed; rendered with | safe.
greece: All the Greek plans swim in warm Aegean or Ionian water, so the split is about vibe and logistics, not temperature. Greece: Ionian Islands is the calmest and easiest — Lefkada and Kefalonia are road- or short-ferry-connected, it stays in one country, and ferry stress is minimal — but it's the least varied. Greek Cyclades is the postcard version: Naxos, Paros and Milos reached by inter-island ferries out of Athens — more iconic and more varied, but exposed to June's meltemi wind and with more moving parts. The other four all center on Crete's Chania coast and differ only in the opener bolted on the front — Portugal's cities, Madeira's levada hiking, the Swiss Alps, or a light Lisbon-and-Athens culture bookend. Crete itself gives the warmest, most family-friendly beaches; the opener is what sets the price, the pace, and how much scenic contrast you get (the Alps opener is the priciest and coldest-starting; Portugal or Madeira add a full hiking or city week; Lisbon keeps it lightest).
portugal: Every Portugal plan opens on the Portuguese side — Cascais and Lisbon, the Algarve, and/or Madeira — so the real choice is the warm-water second leg, or whether to have one at all. Portugal Algarve & Madeira stays entirely Portuguese: the best value and the fewest transfers, but the Atlantic runs cool for swimming. Adding a Mediterranean leg buys warm water at higher cost and a little more travel friction — Mallorca for sandy coves and the easiest swimming, Crete for warm Aegean beaches and Venetian towns, or Sicily for the strongest food and Mount Etna (but the most fragile flights and the lowest ease). The three-stop versions (Algarve + Sicily, Madeira + Sicily) pack in the most but carry the most transfers, and Greece via Lisbon is really a Crete trip with Lisbon and Athens as short cultural bookends.
italy: The Italian plans divide by which Italy you want. Sicily anchors most of them — Cefalù, Taormina, Mount Etna, baroque Ortigia — and brings the board's best food; Sicily & Malta adds Malta's limestone cities and brilliant blue swimming. Sardinia & Corsica trades food and monuments for the best pure swimming: turquoise coves and boat days. Venice, Dolomites & Sardinia is the outlier — high-alpine hiking into a warm-water Sardinia finish, the strongest mountain-to-beach contrast on the board. The rest pair Sicily with a non-Italian opener (Portugal, Madeira, or the Swiss Alps), so the Italian half stays similar while the first week — and the price and flight risk — change. Ease is low across all of them; these are ambitious, transfer-heavy trips.
usa: Both Hawaii plans deliver warm swimming and snorkeling; they differ on islands, length, and cost. Oʻahu + Big Island is the shorter, cheaper, easier version — two islands, volcanoes and waterfalls, nine nights. Maui + Kauai is longer and much pricier: Haleakalā and Hāna on Maui, the Nā Pali Coast and Waimea Canyon on Kauai — more dramatic scenery, but for the most money and time of any plan.
switzerland: Both Swiss plans run the identical five-night Alps opener — Jungfraujoch, the Grindelwald-First cliff walk, Lauterbrunnen's waterfalls — then split on the warm-water finish. Switzerland + Sicily ends with food, baroque towns, and Mount Etna; Switzerland + Crete ends with calmer Aegean swimming on Crete's Chania coast. Sicily is the richer, busier second week; Crete is the simpler, warmer-water one. Both sit among the priciest plans because of the Alps.
